words.ex: Sales increased significantly this year.
use: The new method significantly reduced errors.
words.note: 동사를 꾸미는 부사 — significant(형용사)와 구분!

words.ex: I specifically asked for a window seat.
use: This app was designed specifically for beginners.
mcq: This course is specifically for nurses.
This course is specific for nurses only made.
words.note: specifically for = ~을 위해 특별히. 강조할 때 아주 유용!

words.ex: We have sufficient time to prepare.
use: The evidence wasn't sufficient to prove it.
mcq: The budget is sufficient for the project.
The budget is sufficient to the project.
The budget is sufficiently for project.
words.note: sufficient for + 명사 / sufficient to + 동사. enough의 격식 버전!

words.ex: We need a clear framework for decisions.
mcq: The analysis built a framework we for.
We built framework a the analysis for.
We built a framework for the analysis.
We built a framework to the analysis.
words.note: a framework for + 목적. 전략·분석 문서 단골!

words.ex: The emphasis is on quality, not speed.
use: The course places emphasis on speaking.
mcq: We place emphasis at customer care.
Customer care places emphasis we on.
We place emphasis to customer care.
We place emphasis on customer care.
words.note: place/put emphasis on = ~을 강조하다. 동사는 emphasize!

words.ex: That's equivalent to two days' work.
use: Is there an equivalent word in Korean?
A degree equivalent to a master's.
words.note: equivalent to — to 필수! same as의 격식 버전.

words.ex: The work is virtually finished.
use: It's virtually impossible to book now.
mcq: The plan virtually is complete it.
words.note: virtually = 거의·사실상 / 온라인으로. 두 뜻 다 자주 써요!

words.ex: We received numerous complaints.
use: There are numerous ways to do this.
mcq: This idea numerous studies support it.
words.note: numerous + 복수명사. many의 격식 버전 — 보고서에 딱!

words.ex: We need to evaluate the results.
mcq: We evaluated to each proposal carefully.
We evaluated about each proposal carefully.
words.note: evaluate + 대상 바로. assess와 비슷한 평가 동사!

words.ex: How can you justify the cost?
use: You don't have to justify your choice.
mcq: He tried to justify for his decision.
He tried justifying to his decision.
He tried to justify his decision.
He tried to justify about his decision.
words.note: justify + 대상 바로. 명사는 justification!

words.ex: The parts must fit precisely.
use: Cut the panel precisely to size.
words.note: precisely(부사)가 동사를 꾸며요. 시공 품질 얘기에 딱!

words.ex: Sleep affects cognitive performance.
words.note: cognitive = 인지의. 교육·심리 분야 핵심 형용사!

words.ex: She asserted that she was right.
use: Learn to assert yourself at work.
회사에서 자기 의견을 분명히 표현하는 법을 배우세요.
mcq: You need to asserting yourself more.
You need to assert of yourself more.
You need to assert yourself more.
You need assert to yourself more.
words.note: assert yourself = 당당하게 자기 주장을 하다. 형용사 assertive!

words.ex: I want to do meaningful work.
use: 작은 변화도 의미 있을 수 있다.
mcq: It was a meaningless full experience.
words.note: meaningful ↔ meaningless. 반대말 세트로 기억!

words.ex: She made a tremendous effort.
use: The project was a tremendous success.
It puts tremendous pressure on teachers.
words.note: tremendous = huge의 감정 실린 버전. 칭찬·강조에!

words.ex: That's a legitimate concern.
use: She has a legitimate reason to complain.
그녀가 불만을 가질 정당한 이유가 있다.
words.note: legitimate = 정당한·합법적인. 회의에서 반대 의견을 인정할 때 세련된 단어!

words.ex: We utilize visual aids in every lesson.
words.exko: 저희는 모든 수업에 시각 자료를 활용해요.
use: The app utilizes AI to adjust difficulty.
그 앱은 AI를 활용해 난이도를 조절한다.
Utilize your strengths in the interview.
mcq: Teachers utilize games to engage students.
Teachers utilize of games to engage.
words.note: utilize = use의 격식 버전. 보고서·계획서에서 빛나는 단어!

words.ex: There's a subtle difference between the two.
use: The perfume has a subtle scent.
He gave me a subtle hint.
mcq: The change was subtly but important.
The change was subtle but important.
words.note: subtle — b는 묵음! /서틀/로 발음해요. 4단계에서 도전해 보세요.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with dyslexia at seven.
words.exko: 그는 일곱 살에 난독증 진단을 받았어요.
use: Early diagnosis makes a huge difference.
The doctor diagnosed the problem quickly.
mcq: ADHD diagnosed her with last year.
She diagnosed ADHD to her last year.
She was diagnosed with ADHD last year.
She was diagnosed by ADHD last year.
words.note: be diagnosed with + 질환명. 특수교육 서류·상담의 핵심 표현!

words.ex: It was a seemingly simple question.
use: Seemingly small habits shape big outcomes.
사소해 보이는 습관이 큰 결과를 만든다.
The seemingly shy student loves the stage.
수줍어 보이는 그 학생이 무대를 좋아한다.
mcq: The task seemingly was easy tricking.
The task was seemingly easy but tricky.
The task was seeming easy but tricky.
Seemingly the easy task but was tricky.
words.note: seemingly + 형용사 = 겉보기엔 ~한. 반전을 만들 때 쓰는 부사!

words.ex: She overcame her fear of speaking.
words.note: overcome + 대상. overcome-overcame-overcome!

words.ex: It took time to adapt to the new job.
words.exko: 새 일에 적응하는 데 시간이 걸렸어요.
use: The book was adapted into a film.
mcq: She adapted quickly the new team.
She adapted quickly with the new team.
She adopted quickly to the new team.
She adapted quickly to the new team.
words.note: adapt to = ~에 적응하다. adopt(입양·채택)와 철자 혼동 주의!

words.ex: Her presentation impressed everyone.
use: I was impressed by his patience.
Don't try too hard to impress.
mcq: I was impressed with the service.
I was impressive with the service.
I was impressed to the service.
words.note: be impressed with/by = 감명받다. impressive는 '인상적인'(대상)!

words.ex: I'm confident we'll finish on time.
use: She sounds confident on the phone.
mcq: I'm confident of about the result.
words.note: confident about/in. confidence는 명사!

words.ex: The kids behaved well today.
mcq: The students behaved themselves well good.
words.note: behave (well/badly). 명사는 behavior!

words.ex: I apologize for the delay.
words.note: apologize to 사람 for 이유. 미국식 z, 영국식 s!

words.ex: I really admire your patience.
use: We stopped to admire the view.
mcq: I admire to her for her honesty.
I admire her for her honesty.
I admire her by her honesty.
words.note: admire + 사람 + for + 이유. respect보다 감정이 담긴 단어!

words.ex: How did she react to the news?
use: My skin reacts badly to this cream.
이 크림에 피부가 안 좋게 반응한다.
mcq: He reacted calmly to the criticism.
He reacted calm to the criticism.
He reacted calmly at the criticism.
words.note: react to + 대상. 명사는 reaction!

words.ex: I exercise regularly.
mcq: She regularly checks her email regular.
She checks regularly her the email.
words.note: regularly(부사). regular(형용사)와 구분!

words.ex: Convert the file to PDF.
use: We converted the garage into an office.
How many visitors convert to buyers?
방문자 중 몇 명이 구매자로 전환되나요?
words.note: convert A into/to B. 마케팅 '전환(conversion)'도 이 단어!

words.ex: It was a pleasant surprise.
use: The weather was pleasant all week.
words.note: pleasant(기분 좋게 하는·대상) vs pleased(기쁜·사람)!

words.ex: I'm anxious about the results.
mcq: He's anxious for about the interview.
words.note: anxious about = 걱정되는 / anxious to = 간절히 ~하고 싶은. 두 뜻!

words.ex: I couldn't resist the cake.
use: Resist the urge to check your phone.
mcq: I can't resist eating to chocolate.
words.note: resist + 대상 / resist -ing. can't resist = 못 참겠다!

words.ex: Don't embarrass me in front of them.
words.exko: 그 사람들 앞에서 나 창피하게 하지 마.
mcq: I was embarrassed of my mistake.
I was embarrassed by my mistake.
I was embarrassing by my mistake.
words.note: embarrassed(창피한·사람) vs embarrassing(창피하게 하는·상황). rr·ss 둘 다!

words.ex: I disagree with that decision.
use: We can disagree and still be friends.
mcq: I disagree with you on this.
I am disagree with you on this.
I disagree to you on this.
words.note: disagree with + 사람/의견. be동사 없이!

words.ex: Thanks for the insight.
use: The data gave us new insights.
She has great insight into customers.
mcq: The report offers insight to the market.
The report offers insight of the market.
The report offers insight into the market.
The report offers insight for the market.
words.note: insight into = ~에 대한 통찰. 회의·보고서 고급 단어!

words.ex: I'm curious about your plan.
use: Just curious — how old are you?
words.note: curious about = ~이 궁금한. Just curious = 그냥 궁금해서!

words.ex: Don't pretend you didn't hear me.
words.note: pretend to + 동사 = ~인 척하다.

words.ex: My boss is very strict about deadlines.
words.note: strict about/with = ~에 엄격한.

words.ex: Give me a hint!
use: He dropped a hint about a promotion.
mcq: She hinted about that she might leave.
She hinted that she might leave.
She hinted she might to leave.
words.note: hint (that) = 넌지시 말하다. drop a hint = 암시를 흘리다!
